about.title: Personal Injury Help in St. Helena, California
about.longDescription: St. Helena is a small city, but its streets still see their share of collisions. In the most recent year with finalized public records, 2016, the city logged 24 injury collisions and 31 people hurt — thankfully with zero traffic deaths that year. Local roads like Main Street, Rt 29, Oak Avenue, and Silverado Trail see the bulk of reported crashes, and Thursdays between noon and 2 p.m. tend to be when reports cluster. If you were hurt in a crash on any of these roads, or anywhere else around town, it helps to understand your options early — especially since California gives most injury victims only two years to file a claim, and less time if a government entity is involved. We handle personal injury cases for people hurt in St. Helena and throughout Napa County. We review your situation at no cost, and we only get paid if you recover money.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can mean losing your right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit how much you can recover for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses. We can help make sure that side of your claim isn't overlooked.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless You Win
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless we recover money for you. That structure exists so cost isn't a barrier to getting advice.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in St. Helena?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury claim. If your accident involved a government vehicle or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery is simply reduced by the percentage of fault assigned to you.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in St. Helena?
items.answer: Public crash records show that reported collisions in St. Helena concentrate along corridors like Main Street, Rt 29, Oak Avenue, and Silverado Trail, with Thursdays around midday showing more reports than other times. These are simply patterns from public records, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims for clients in St. Helena and Napa County. We represent injured people and work directly on your case. We don't charge upfront fees — we only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Will I owe anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Our initial case review is free. If you decide to work with us, we handle your case on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover compensation for you.
